themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 8 this week versus a 2.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 256% increase (z-score: 4.8)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or inadequate removal in the district this week.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score: 4.8)
Statistically significant deviation meeting high-severity threshold
Emerging pattern suggests recent outbreak rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: photograph locations of graffiti, interview residents and business owners about frequency and locations
City response: contact DSNY and local council member's office about removal timelines and whether a specific neighborhood corridor is targeted

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes piling up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 3 this week from a 0.5-complaint weekly baseline—a 500% spike (z-score: 3.54)—indicating a sudden accumulation problem on streets that warrants rapid investigation into whether a bike-share system is involved or bikes are being discarded.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Spike is recent and concentrated, not a long-running pattern
Suggests acute event (system outage, illegal dumping) rather than baseline condition
reporting_angles: Micro-reporting: locate and photograph the three complaint sites; interview neighbors about when bikes appeared and condition
System angle: check whether Citi Bike or another service has a rebalancing or mechanical issue, or if private bikes are being abandoned

themes_detail.label: Bus shelter infrastructure gaps
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter placement complaints exploded to 3 two weeks ago from a 0.1-complaint weekly average—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity score)—suggesting a recent transit infrastructure failure, service cut, or bus route realignment affecting the district.
evidence: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest severity)
Extreme statistical deviation suggests systemic change, not random variation
Affects daily commute experience for residents dependent on transit
reporting_angles: MTA accountability: request records of recent bus stop shelter removals, replacements, or maintenance work in Midwood; interview MTA about decision-making
Resident impact: find and interview the three complainants and neighbors about weather exposure, wait times, and accessibility

themes_detail.label: Dead trees on neighborhood streets
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints rose to 8 last week from a 2.4-complaint weekly average—a 237% increase (z-score: 3.57)—indicating either recent storm damage, disease spread, or a maintenance backlog that is becoming visually acute.
evidence: 8 complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average (237% spike, z-score: 3.57)
Recent weather or disease pressure likely cause (worth investigating timing of complaints relative to storms or pest reports)
Indicates neighborhood canopy health is deteriorating at accelerated rate
reporting_angles: Environmental beat: map the locations of 8 complaints, photograph trees, and assess for common cause (storm damage, pest, disease strain)
City services: contact Parks Department about removal queue, replanting budget, and timeline for the district

themes_detail.label: Air quality concerns emerging
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago from a 0.6-complaint weekly average—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting either a localized pollution source, industrial emissions, or construction activity that residents are noticing and reporting for the first time.
evidence: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Statistically significant and unusual for this district
Could indicate new construction dust, traffic changes, or industrial emission event
reporting_angles: Source investigation: cross-reference 4 complaints with DOB permit filings (359 alterations filed recently) and industrial facilities; conduct air sampling if possible
Health angle: contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and local health department about air monitoring; interview complainants about symptoms or observations
